title: A scalar finite-volume criterion for a continuum mass gap in SU(2) lattice gauge theory: the doubling test in dimensions four and three, its continuum assembly and its converse (note v1.3)
description:
A scalar finite-volume criterion for a continuum mass gap in SU(2) lattice gauge theory (note v1.3, 12 November 2026). Version 1.3 adds two sections of theory (flux sectors and ’t Hooft twists; failure of the criterion at every fixed lattice size as the coupling tends to infinity) and two abstract Lean files; the statements, proofs and Lean files of versions 1.0 to 1.2 are unchanged. No simulation data.

Version 1.3 (this version). (1) Flux sectors and ’t Hooft twists. For Wilson’s SU(2) theory the periodic trace splits exactly over the electric-flux sectors; the criterion Δ(n) ≤ 2−9 at one size implies disorder of the ’t Hooft twists, 0 ≤ 1 − Zk/Z0 ≤ qN/n/124, on every hypercube of side N ≥ n — a bound growing like a length, not an area, from which no area law in infinite volume follows; the criterion is equivalent, up to constants, to two one-scale inequalities (twist disorder and a neutral-sector bound), each failed by a different model; a necessary growth of n with β is derived conditionally on Theorem 7.59 of Bhattacharjee et al. (v5.0.0). (2) The criterion fails at every fixed lattice size as β → ∞. The twist ratio of SU(2) on a fixed torus is bounded by a power of β (Laplace’s method on isolated twisted vacua), that of U(1) and Z2 decays exponentially, and liminf Δβ(n) ≥ 45 log 2 at every n ≥ 3. This says where the criterion fails; it is not a mass-gap result; the constants are not explicit; the ingredients are classical, no novelty is claimed for the asymptotics, and anteriority is not settled. The proofs are on paper and were checked by AI models only. The two new Lean files check abstract finite algebra only (the analytic part is not formalised). Hypothesis (C) for Wilson’s theory rests on the paper proof of the author’s tube-and-bridge note (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24153930). Written by AI models and read by other AI models; no human has checked the proofs.

What the note is. A technical note that transposes the two-dimensional finite-volume doubling criterion of OpenAI (Proposition 2.2 of “Sharp mass bounds for the two-dimensional O(4) model”, 23 September 2026) to lattice gauge theories in dimensions four and three. It is predominantly a transposition, not a new mass-gap mechanism; no priority is claimed for the mechanism.

Results. For the SU(2) Wilson action on periodic tori, set Δβ(n) = 16 log Z(n4) − log Z((2n)4). Under hypercubic symmetry and a positive trace-class transfer representation (a hypothesis, not formalised), Δ(n) ≤ 2−9 implies Δ(2n) ≤ 256 Δ(n)2 and (λi/λ0)n ≤ 256 Δ(n) ≤ 1/2 on every spatial torus (2jn)3 (in dimension three: 2−7 and 64). If Δβk(nk) ≤ η ≤ 2−9 along lattices of spacing ak = ℓ/nk and the lattice Osterwalder–Schrader forms converge (the existence of the continuum limit, assumed), the limit satisfies the q-form of the gap with q = 256η; under the Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction (also assumed) its mass gap is at least −log(256η)/ℓ ≥ (log 2)/ℓ and its vacuum is unique. This implication is formalised in Lean 4 (35 declarations, standard axioms only) against the author’s own Lean statement of the problem (ClayYM v1.1, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23644079), with the transfer representation, the convergence and the reconstruction as named hypotheses. A converse (finite-volume gap including electric-flux sectors, plus a trace bound) is proved on paper at a fixed physical size, with counterexamples when either ingredient is dropped.

Status. The Lean sources were rebuilt on 11 November 2026 by a non-author on a clean machine from hashed copies, and again from the git archive of this package (see the note, Appendix A). The torus–cylinder comparison, the converse and the witnesses are proved on paper only. The strong-coupling instance (Δβ(2) ≤ 1.741·10−3 for β ≤ 0.005) is conditional on a finite enumeration and a rational comparison reported from one program and not independently certified. The Maxwell witness is conditional on an identification with a normalised Villain measure that is not derived; the massive-scalar thresholds are numerical. Written by AI models and read by other AI models; no human has checked the proofs; not refereed.

Relation to earlier public work. Version 5.0.0 of the series of Bhattacharjee et al. (The Yang-Mills Mass Gap from One Bound at One Scale, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24147967; record created on 11 November 2026, before version 1.0 of this note) contains, for four-dimensional tori, the same doubling defect, its bracket by thermal traces, the purity reading, and a one-scale criterion (B*) whose hypothesis implies ours. Version 1.2 proved the reverse implication (Theorem R): under symmetry and a positive transfer representation, Δ(n) ≤ 2−9 implies (B*) at the scale 16n and the gap (log 2)/n on every integer cube of side N ≥ n; the two criteria are equivalent up to a change of scale (a factor 16 in the reverse direction, 32 for a round trip; 16 is not optimal). Positivity of the transfer operator is indispensable (example with Δ < 0). A corollary to their Theorem F is conditional on their hypothesis (W) and their Theorem F as we read them, and not verified by us. This does not answer a question left open in their text (their datum differs from ours) and is not a proof of the mass gap. No priority is claimed for the one-scale criterion, the defect or the monotonicity of the free energy in a period (classical).

Version 1.1 (literature corrections, previous version). The note now records that the principle “an inequality between partition functions of finite periodic tori (twisted against untwisted) implies decay” is classical (Tomboulis–Yaffe 1985; Kovács–Tomboulis 2002, eq. (11); Kanazawa 2008, Theorems 1, 2 and 5), and adds a comparison with these papers: same family of argument (reflection positivity, doublings), different hypothesis (insensitivity to a centre twist, not the doubling defect) and different conclusion (Wilson loops or spin correlations of a periodic box, not a bound on the transfer matrix of every spatial torus). Version 1.0 remains available as its own record.

Limitations. No estimate of Δ at weak coupling, no existence or non-triviality of the continuum limit, no reconstruction. The criterion does not apply as it stands to the formalised construction of OpenAI (Section 12 of the note). Reading Δ as a combination of Rényi-2 entropies of the thermal weights is a reformulation, not a result. The criterion is a sufficient condition; its equivalence with the Yang–Mills mass-gap problem is not claimed. The anteriority search is limited and recorded in the note.
